record.paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Given that most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, how should heterogeneous computing mapping procedures incorporate multi-tasking, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage multi-tasking together with other quality-of-service requirements?

evidence.quote: Incorporating multi-tasking is an area of ongoing HC research.

Most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, but how to incorporate this into the mapping process, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage this capability with other QoS requirements is being investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing system consisting of a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \dots, m_p\}$ with differing architectures and capabilities, and a stream of arriving tasks $T = \{t_1, t_2, \dots\}$. Each task $t_i$ has, on each machine $m_j$, an estimated execution time $e_{ij}$, a deadline $d_i$, and possibly other quality-of-service (QoS) parameters (priority, throughput, security level, accuracy tolerance). Each machine $m_j$ runs a multi-tasking operating system that can time-share its processor among multiple tasks simultaneously according to a scheduling discipline (e.g., a quantum-based round-robin or weighted fair-share policy parameterized by per-task weights $w_{ij} \ge 0$).

A mapping/scheduling procedure must produce, online or offline, both (i) an assignment of each task $t_i$ to one or more machines and (ii) for each machine $m_j$, a vector of time-share weights $(w_{ij})_i$ (with $\sum_i w_{ij} \le 1$ at any instant) governing how the operating system multi-tasks the assigned tasks.

Develop and analyze a mapping procedure that explicitly incorporates per-processor multi-tasking — that is, jointly determines task-to-machine assignment and processor time-allocation among coexisting tasks — while satisfying a specified collection of QoS constraints, and provide performance guarantees (e.g., on makespan, deadline-miss ratio, or QoS satisfaction) relative to a clairvoyant optimum. In particular, characterize how the freedom to share each processor among multiple tasks should be exploited to improve overall QoS compared with non-preemptive single-task-per-processor mappings, and identify conditions under which multi-tasking is provably beneficial or harmful.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research direction in heterogeneous computing rather than a single sharply-posed problem with a yes/no answer. Multi-tasking-aware mapping with QoS continues to be an active area in heterogeneous and cloud/edge scheduling research, with no definitive resolution; many heuristics and approximation results exist for restricted formulations, but a general solution remains absent.

status_evidence.title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists multi-tasking incorporation into HC mapping as an open research area.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem is identified as ongoing/open research in heterogeneous computing.
